_doc: BRAIN HUNTER s14 (2026-08-29). Sections 1-3 of arXiv:1601.00991 '101 Formulaic Alphas' (Kakushadze 2015) -- the EMPIRICAL half s13 could not extract. Recovered by GID-block calibration (data/brain_hunter_s14_gid_recover.py + brain_hunter_s14_anchors.json) after establishing that no font-level Unicode channel survives in the file. Numbers are the PAPER'S claims about US equities 2015; they are ore, never evidence for this desk.

source.population: 101 alphas, US equities, delay-0 and delay-1

table_1_summary._note: row label -> [min, q1, median, mean, q3, max]

table_2_ln_R_on_ln_sigma.note: from Figure 2's printed fit; Table 2's own body is the two-regressor block

table_4_rho_ij_on_y_ij_and_z_ij._the_finding: adjusted R-squared 0.0123 over 5050 pairs. BOTH regressors are 'significant' (t 2.9, 7.5) and together explain 1.2% of alpha correlation. This is the canonical large-n significance-without-explanatory-power result, printed by the paper about its own corpus.

mechanism_extracted.the_turnover_premium_is_a_volatility_pro: Table 5 says higher-turnover alphas are more volatile (ln sigma ~ 0.368 ln T, R2 0.228). Table 2 says return scales with volatility (ln R ~ 0.761 ln sigma). Compose and turnover LOOKS like it pays: R ~ T^0.28. Table 3 runs both together and turnover collapses to t = -0.57. The turnover premium is pass-through, not residual -- the same shape as a lag-0 control. Any desk that sizes on a turnover/holding-period return relationship without a volatility control is double-counting volatility.
mechanism_extracted.mean_correlation_hides_the_maximum: The paper's abstract headline is 'average pair-wise correlation is low, 15.9%'. Its own Table 1 reports the MAXIMUM pair-wise correlation at 87.33%. A corpus advertised as 101 alphas is not 101 independent bets, and the paper says so in the row nobody quotes. Anyone porting alpha101 and counting 101 toward orthogonality or toward a trial count is wrong by the paper's own measurement.
mechanism_extracted.the_corpus_dispersion_is_volatility_not_: Annualized return spans 3.285%-28.72% (8.7x) while Sharpe spans 1.238-4.162 (3.4x). Most of the return dispersion across the 101 is volatility dispersion. Ranking ported alphas by return ranks them mostly by volatility.
mechanism_extracted.the_cost_line: Median cents-per-share 0.397 at a median 2.1-day holding period. The corpus's economics assume a thousands-of-names cross-section traded at sub-cent frictions. An MT5 CFD book has neither the cross-section nor the cost structure; the SHARPE numbers do not transfer, the HOLDING-PERIOD distribution (median 2.1d, min 0.62d) is the transferable quantity.

not_recovered: Figure 1/3/4 are raster plots (no text). Sections 3.2's factor-model equation (7) still carries unmapped Greek GIDs -- named, not guessed.
